lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Byłaś|bylas już w tym nowym|nowym kinie|kinie na Woli|woli?
lines.en: Have you been to that new cinema in Wola yet?

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Jeszcze nie. Poszłabym|poszlabym, ale w tym tygodniu|tygodniu napisałam|napisalam pięć raportów|raportow i nie mam siły|sily.
lines.en: Not yet. I’d go, but I’ve written five reports this week and I’m worn out.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: To może w sobotę|sobote? Gdybyś|gdybys chciała|chciala, poszlibyśmy|poszlibysmy razem.
lines.en: Saturday, then? If you wanted, we could go together.

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Chętnie! Mógłbyś|moglbys kupić bilety? Ja bym|bym zapomniała|zapomniala.
lines.en: I’d love to! Could you get the tickets? I’d forget.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Jasne. Moi koledzy|koledzy już tam byli|byli i mówili|mowili, że jest świetne|swietne.
lines.en: Sure. My friends have already been and said it’s great.

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.en: That would be the perfect end to the week.

bylas.why: Tomek is asking Ania, so the verb agrees with her. In a “you” form, the gender marker follows the person you’re talking to.

nowym.why: Adjectives copy the case, number and gender of their noun. Kino is neuter and in the locative here, so nowy becomes nowym.

parts: loc. sg. -e (the i marks n softened to ń)
kinie.why: W + locative means “in” a place. The locative ending -e softens the n to ń, which is spelled ni before a vowel: kino → kinie.
kinie.compare: Going there takes a different case: idę do kina.

woli.why: Many Warsaw districts take na instead of w: na Woli, na Mokotowie, na Pradze.
woli.history: From wola, “will, freedom”: an old name for new settlements granted some years free of dues to attract settlers.

poszlabym.tags: verb · perfective · conditional · 1st person singular · feminine
parts: root of iść, past-tense form (cf. szedł)
poszlabym.why: The conditional is the past form without its person marker (poszła) plus by plus a person marker. Ania uses it to say she’d like to go, and ale tells you what’s stopping her.
poszlabym.compare: Same meaning, marker detached: Ja bym poszła.

you.f: You would say: poszłabym, as Ania does.

tygodniu.why: W tym tygodniu = “this week.” The stem shifts from tydzień to tygodni- everywhere except the nominative and accusative singular.
tygodniu.history: From an old phrase meaning “that day”: the period until the same weekday comes round again.

napisalam.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person singular · feminine
napisalam.why: Ania is talking about herself, so her past-tense “I” form carries the feminine -a-. The perfective (na- + pisać) says the five reports are finished.

you.f: You would say: napisałam, as Ania does.

raportow.why: Numbers from 5 up take the genitive plural. With 2–4 you get the ordinary plural: trzy raporty.

sily.why: Negating a verb turns its direct object genitive: mam siłę → nie mam siły. The phrase is the everyday way to say “I’m worn out.”

sobote.why: Days of the week take w + accusative: w sobotę, w poniedziałek.
sobote.history: Ultimately from Hebrew shabbat, which reached Slavic through Greek.

gdybys.why: In a hypothetical if-clause the person ending moves onto gdyby and the verb stays bare: gdybyś chciała, not gdyby chciałaś.

chciala.why: The e of chcieć alternates with a before the past suffix: chcieć → chciał. The gender follows Ania, the person being asked.

poszlibysmy.tags: verb · perfective · conditional · 1st person plural · virile
poszlibysmy.why: The virile ending -i is used because the group, Tomek and Ania, includes a man; before it, ł is written l. One man in a group is enough.

you.m: Any group you’re part of: poszlibyśmy.
you.f: With a mixed group: poszlibyśmy. With only women: poszłybyśmy.

moglbys.tags: verb · imperfective · conditional · 2nd person singular · masculine
moglbys.why: The conditional of móc is the standard polite request, like English “could you.” It’s masculine because Ania is asking Tomek. The root has ó in a closed syllable (móc, mógł, mógłbyś) and o when a vowel follows (mogła, mogli, mogę).
moglbys.compare: To a woman: Mogłabyś kupić bilety?

bym.why: The conditional particle with its person marker can detach from the verb and attach to an earlier word in the clause, here ja. Ja bym zapomniała and zapomniałabym mean the same; the overt ja is contrastive: “I’m the one who’d forget.”

zapomniala.why: This is the verb half of a detached conditional (ja bym … zapomniała). As in chcieć → chciała, the e of the infinitive alternates with a before the past suffix.
zapomniala.history: Za- plus an old verb pomnieć, “to remember,” which survives in pomnik “monument” and wspomnieć “to recall.”

you.m: You would say: ja bym zapomniał.
you.f: You would say: ja bym zapomniała.

koledzy.why: Nouns for male persons have a special nominative plural, and it softens the stem consonant: kolega → koledzy, like drogi → drodzy.

byli.why: Tomek’s friends are men, so the plural takes the virile ending -i; before it, ł is written l.

mowili.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 3rd person plural · virile
mowili.why: Same agreement as byli. Reported talk usually takes imperfective mówić; powiedzieli would point to one specific occasion.

swietne.why: The unspoken subject is kino, which is neuter, so the adjective is neuter too: jest świetne.
swietne.history: Related to świat and światło, “light,” and świecić, “to shine”: originally “bright, shining.”

byloby.why: The neuter ending -o agrees with the subject to, “that.” The by at the start is the stem of być; the by at the end is the conditional particle. Third person has no person marker.
byloby.compare: With a feminine subject: To byłaby dobra kolacja.

explain.m: The masculine has no agreement ending: kupi + ł + by + m.
explain.f: Built like Ania’s poszłabym: kupi + ł + a + by + m.

exercises.hint: Look at how poszłabym is put together, then check the learner setting at the top.

exercises.prompt: You and a male friend: “we would do it” (zrobić).
exercises.explain: A group with a man takes the virile ending -i, and ł is written l before it: zrobi + l + i + by + śmy.
exercises.hint: Who’s in the group? One man makes the plural virile.

exercises.explain: With the feminine ending -a after it, the syllable opens and ó becomes o: mog + ł + a + by + ś.
exercises.hint: Tomek gets mógłbyś. What changes for a woman, and what happens to the ó?

exercises.prompt: “That would cost a lot”: To ___ dużo (kosztować).
exercises.explain: The neuter ending -o agrees with to, then by with no person marker, as in byłoby.
exercises.hint: The subject is to. Which gender is it, and does it need a person ending?
